newsitem.title: CANADA: Director and actor defend new IRA film as accurate.
newsitem.headline: Director and actor defend new IRA film as accurate.

text.p: Dublin-born director Neil Jordan defended on Friday his heroic portrayal of Irish nationalist Michael Collins in his new IRA movie starring Liam Neeson.

"I did see a heroic element to Collins that I wouldn't make any apologies for," Jordan told reporters at a news conference one day after its North American premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival.
Jordan shot down critics of the film who called it historically inaccurate and who said it perpetuated the mythical stature of Collins.
"The film is as accurate as I could make it and I did study history so I do know what that entails," said Jordan, who also directed the acclaimed Irish film "The Crying Game."

Collins fought to end British rule in Ireland in the Easter Uprising of 1916, waged guerrilla war against the British with an forerunner of the IRA. He later broke with his comrades over the partition of Ireland and was killed in an IRA ambush in 1922.

Jordan said he had not shown the picture to the head of the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams, but that many conservative British journalists who have seen the picture praised it as an "accurate account."
Actor Aidan Quinn, who also stars in the movie, said the controversial Irish figure may be gaining some of the recognition he deserves.
"Michael Collins when I was in school in Dublin was kind of a footnote at that time," Quinn said. "It has since changed. He kind of got shafted by history."
Jordan and the film's producer, Stephen Woolley, said the movie was filmed entirely in Ireland and under the watchful eyes of people who are very familiar with the people and the story.
They said English actor Alan Ryckman, who played Irish Preident Eamon Devalare in the movie, had to act his first scene in front of thousands of spectators.
"His first performance on film was reviewed ... in the Irish Times," Woolley said.
"Michael Collins" won the Golden Lion award at the Venice Film Festival and captured the best actor trophy at Venice for Liam Neeson's in the title role.
